post.title: 409 S&P 500 companies pay owners cash. Here's how
post.ig:
409 S&P 500 companies pay owners cash. That cash is a dividend.

409 of the S&P 500's companies (81.3%) paid a dividend as of Q4 2025.
Own the stock before the ex-dividend date (now the same day as the record date); cash arrives on the payment date.
Example: 100 shares x $0.50 a quarter = $50 a quarter, $200 a year. Yield = yearly dividend / price, so $2 on a $50 share = 4%.
The S&P 500 paid a record $78.92 a share in 2025, but dividends aren't guaranteed: Intel suspended its dividend starting Q4 2024. From 1940-2024, dividends averaged 34% of the S&P 500's total return.

Sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices (Jan 2026); Hartford Funds; Intel (Aug 2024); FINRA.

A dividend is a slice of company profit paid to shareholders; 409 S&P 500 companies paid one as of Q4 2025, and the index paid a record $78.92 a share in 2025. Dividends aren't guaranteed (Intel suspended its dividend starting Q4 2024), yet from 1940-2024 they averaged 34% of the S&P 500's total return. Sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices, Hartford Funds, Intel. News and education, not financial advice.
